name: Fairmont St. Andrews
insider_take: Where legendary golf meets Scottish grandeur – this is your gateway to the home of golf itself.
whats_special: Built on a cliff overlooking the North Sea, Fairmont St. Andrews sits just minutes from the legendary Old Course where golf was born over 600 years ago. The hotel features two championship golf courses designed by Bruce Devlin and offers unparalleled views of St. Andrews Bay. You're staying in the town that's home to Scotland's oldest university (founded 1413) and where Prince William and Kate Middleton first met.
pro_tip: Book tee times at the Old Course well in advance – it's a ballot system for non-members, but the hotel's concierge can help secure coveted spots on this bucket-list course.
dont_miss: Walking across the iconic Swilcan Bridge on the 18th hole of the Old Course, exploring the medieval ruins of St. Andrews Cathedral, and experiencing the dramatic coastal walk along the Fife Coastal Path. The town's cobblestone streets are steeped in 900 years of history – from golf's birthplace to royal romance.
pros: Two championship golf courses on-site including the famous Torrance Course
Stunning clifftop location overlooking St. Andrews Bay and the North Sea
Historic town of St. Andrews with Old Course and university nearby
Luxury spa and extensive leisure facilities
cons: Remote location requires transportation to reach town center
Premium pricing reflects luxury positioning and golf resort status
